sources.fullCitation: Sara Janina Lengowski. “Moritz Mayer-Mahr.” In Lexikon verfolgter Musiker und Musikerinnen der NS-Zeit, edited by Claudia Maurer Zenck and Peter Petersen. Hamburg: Universität Hamburg, 2006, updated 11 December 2025.
sources.publication: Lexikon verfolgter Musiker und Musikerinnen der NS-Zeit
sources.title: LexM — Mayer-Mahr, Moritz
sources.researchNote: The live LexM entry documents Mayer-Mahr’s teaching at the Klindworth-Scharwenka Conservatory in Berlin from 1892 to 1937, his service from 1907 on the jury of the Ibach competition at the Stern Conservatory, and his work until 1933 on the senate of the Academy of Arts as an expert in music pedagogy. It names Róża Etkin among his pupils. An earlier PDF copy hosted by the Xaver-Scharwenka-Stiftung is retained as an alternate access copy.

sources.fullCitation: Sophie Fetthauer. “Viktor Alberti.” In Lexikon verfolgter Musiker und Musikerinnen der NS-Zeit, edited by Claudia Maurer Zenck, Peter Petersen, Sophie Fetthauer and Friedrich Geiger. Hamburg: Universität Hamburg, 2022, updated 1 December 2025.
sources.title: LexM — Alberti, Viktor
sources.creator: Sophie Fetthauer
sources.publication: Lexikon verfolgter Musiker und Musikerinnen der NS-Zeit
sources.researchNote: Identifies the Alberti firm behind nineteen of the registered works: the music and theatre publishing house of Viktor Alberti (Miskolc 1884 – Melbourne 1942), a Hungarian-born publisher and music dealer working in Berlin, whose house issued the first German jazz periodical, Musik-Echo, from 1930 to 1934. The entry settles an identification the name registers do not: the GND carries only Max Alberti’s Verlag of Hanau, a different house.
